layman_headline: Fear lingers in the crypto market — no clean swing trade setups worth the risk right now.
layman_explanation: The crypto market is sitting in 'Fear' territory at 27 out of 100, and that fear has been worsening over the past week. Bitcoin is holding around $64,000 with Glassnode flagging $63,000 as a key battleground. The swing trade candidates on the watchlist are either low-quality micro-caps with missing data (no RSI, no chart analysis, no funding rates) or have already run up sharply and look extended. With Bitcoin dominance high at 56.6%, altcoins are struggling to outperform, making it a tough environment for alt swing trades.
layman_action: Stay patient and keep your cash ready. The market mood is fearful but not panicked enough to signal a clear contrarian buy, and the available trade setups lack the data quality needed to enter with confidence. Wait for a cleaner opportunity.
expert_reasoning: Applying validated rules: Fear & Greed at 27 is just above the 25 threshold where Rule #3 says the outlook is 'genuinely ambiguous.' The trend is worsening (yesterday was 25, week avg 26.7). Per Rule #4, I need at least three core data sources working — while I do have price data, news, and Fear & Greed, the swing candidates themselves are severely data-deficient: only 2 of 7 have RSI readings, none have funding rates, and only 2 have chart analysis. RSI is my most reliable signal (71% win rate per signal credibility data), and it reads neutral (55-56) on the two coins that have it. BTC dominance at 56.6% actively suppresses altcoin performance. UB's -33% daily drop contradicts its bullish chart pattern, suggesting either a rug pull risk or stale chart data. BTW and PUMP have already run 43% and 22% in 7 days respectively — chasing these violates swing trading discipline. DEXE and ETHFI are down 95%+ from ATH with no chart data to identify support levels. The prudent action is to HOLD and wait for a setup with confirming signals across multiple reliable indicators.
risk_factors: Fear & Greed could deteriorate below 25, triggering broader selling and dragging BTC below the $63,000 support level Glassnode identified
High BTC dominance (56.6%) means any market weakness disproportionately crushes altcoins — the exact category of our swing candidates
Most swing candidates are micro-cap tokens with severe data gaps, making any entry essentially a blind bet
watch_list: Fear & Greed Index — if it drops to 25 or below, expect continued downward drift per Rule #7; if it recovers above 35, the environment improves for entries
Bitcoin price action around $63,000 support — a breakdown could cascade into altcoin selling, while a strong bounce could create real opportunities
ADA's +18.1% weekly move — if it consolidates with rising volume rather than reversing, it could become a valid swing candidate on the next cycle
market_context: The crypto market is in a fearful but not panicked state, with BTC holding $64K amid institutional news flow around stablecoins and tokenization. High BTC dominance (56.6%) signals capital is rotating into Bitcoin and away from alts, making this a poor environment for altcoin swing trades.
context_banner: Market fear is rising and altcoin candidates lack sufficient data for a high-conviction entry — capital preservation is the best trade today.

key_signals.description: Fear & Greed at 27 with a worsening weekly trend (yesterday 25, avg 26.7) — not yet at the extreme-fear levels that historically precede bounces, but close enough to demand caution.
The only two candidates with RSI data (UB at 55.8, PUMP at 56.2) both read neutral, providing no oversold bounce signal — and RSI is our most reliable indicator at 71% win rate.
Glassnode identifies Bitcoin's $63,000 zone as a key buyer battleground — if this level breaks, altcoins will suffer disproportionately given high BTC dominance.
BNY offering institutional crypto staking and US-UK stablecoin regulatory support are positive long-term but not generating immediate altcoin price catalysts.
No volume-vs-average data available for any swing candidate, making it impossible to confirm breakout quality — a critical missing signal given 60% historical reliability.
